The Azes I page's table lists Zoilos II in the Eastern Punjab column for 55-35 BCE and Hippostratos in Western Punjab for 65-55, and the page gives no Indo-Greek holdings in the Punjab after 35 BCE; the Indo-Scythians page has the Indo-Scythians take 'northwestern India' from Hippostratos in 55 BCE. c. 10 CE: Rajuvula takes Sagala from the last Indo-Greek. 'Rajuvula conquered the last remaining Indo-Greek kingdom, under Strato II, around 10 CE, and took his capital city, Sagala'.

ledger.note: c. 20 CE: Gondophares founds the Indo-Parthian kingdom out of the Saka lands. 'The kingdom was founded in 19/20 when the governor of Drangiana' declared independence; 'Gondophares became the ruler of areas comprising Arachosia, Seistan, Sindh, Punjab, and the Kabul valley', 'perhaps after the death of the important ruler Azes'. The page also says 'Around 20–10 BC, he made conquests in the former Indo-Scythian kingdom, perhaps after the death of the important ruler Azes', which conflicts with its 'founded in 19/20'; 20 CE follows the founding date and the infobox (confidence 1). Sa-02-b repair: the region now includes Arachosia and Seistan. The earlier note said they lay outside Cliopatria's Indo-Scythian shape, which is false: the shapes of 1, 14, 43 and 51 hold Arachosia (540 cells at 14) and Seistan, so the dossier kept them to 74 while indo-parthians gains them in 20 and holds them to 226; keyframes indo-scythians_20, _43 and _51 now take them out from 20. The Western Satraps page, re-read for the repair, gives no event for the cut: it lists 'Established: 35' with 'c. 35: Abhiraka' as first ruler and says the position of modern scholarship is that the Western Satraps were vassals of the Kushans.

ledger.note: c. 51 CE: Kujula Kadphises takes the Kabul and Gandhara country. Hou Hanshu: he 'took the Gaofu (Kabul) region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda (Paktiya) and Jibin (Kapisha and Gandhara)'; the Kushans were 'gradually wresting control of the area from the Scythian tribes'. His reign is dated 25-85 (infobox), c. 30-80 and c. 50-90 on the same page; 51 is Cliopatria's year. The Kujula Kadphises page (read 2026-10-19) gives no year and names a different victim: 'The invasion of the Indo-Parthian kingdom led by Kujula Kadphises is thought to have occurred some time after 45 CE', during the reign of Gondophares's successors Abdagases and Sases, so the lands may be the Indo-Parthians' (the indo-parthians dossier has the loss at 50); the cells are drawn Indo-Scythian in Cliopatria's 43 shape and are kept here.

'Mathura became part of the Kushan Empire from the reign of Vima Kadphises (90-100 CE)'; the satraps were 'probably displaced by, or became vassals of, the Kushans', and Kharapallana and Vanaspara appear as Kanishka's governors at Sarnath in c. 130 CE. The Indo-Scythians page puts the Mathura region at c. 100 CE.

wars.name: Saka invasions of Parthia

wars.note: The page names no zone. The Maues page dates the death of Phraates II to 126 BCE.

wars.outcome: Mithridates II defeated the Indo-Scythians; 'the region of Sakastan was incorporated into the Parthian Empire'; he also seized western Bactria.

wars.name: Maues' conquest of Gandhara and Taxila
wars.outcome: The Sakas took Taxila from Apollodotus II and Pushkalavati from the Indo-Greeks; Maues overstruck Archebius' and Apollodotus II's coins at Taxila.

wars.outcome: Vikrama retook Ujjain from the Indo-Scythians and set up the Vikrama era in 58 BCE (Indo-Scythians page).
wars.note: The page names no state for Vikrama; the Satavahana page's 'Vikramaditya of Ujjain' (78 CE) is a different tradition.

wars.name: Rajuvula's conquest of the last Indo-Greek kingdom
wars.outcome: Rajuvula eliminated Strato II c. 10 CE and took Sagala.

zones.text: Kabul and Gandhara, taken by Kujula Kadphises

notes:
Cliopatria row Indo-Scythians -144..282, 16 shapes. Nine pages opened (budget 9). None gives an infobox area (Indo-Scythians, Indo-Parthian, Western Satraps pages give none), so no area ratio could be computed.

Departures from Cliopatria:
1. The state is ended at 100, not 282. The Indo-Scythians page ends the Mathura satrapy c. 100 CE (Northern Satraps page: Kushan from Vima Kadphises, 90-100 CE). The Cliopatria 91 and 270 shapes (Sistan, 121,799 km2) are marked wrong: the Sakastan page puts Sistan under Parthia from c. 100 BC and the Suren, the Indo-Parthian page says the Indo-Parthians kept Sakastan to c. 224/5, and the Sakastan page makes it a Sasanian province c. 240 with governors Narseh (to 271) and Hormizd (revolt c. 281, put down 283). The one support for the Cliopatria row is a sentence of the Indo-Scythians page: the Indo-Scythians held Sistan until the reign of Bahram II (276-293 CE); pages disagree and I followed the more specific ones. The indo-parthians dossier carries the Sistan cells for 91-224.
2. Shapes -110 and -91 move their boundary from -92/-91 to -101/-100 (Mithridates II, Sakastan page 'around 100 BC').
